title: Delete a node safely
summary: Keep a pointer to the node, unlink it, then delete it.

checkpoints.text: The list now holds 10, 20, 30. `deleteFront` will remove the first node.
`temp` remembers the first node. Without it, the next line would leave nothing pointing at that node.
`head` moves to the second node. The first node is still reachable through `temp`, so it is not leaked.
The node is deleted and its box disappears. `temp` still holds the old address for a moment: it is a dangling pointer, harmless here only because the function returns without using it.
Deleting returns memory; losing the last pointer does not. Open the example called Mistake: losing the head to see the difference.
